newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Kiwi Gold s/holders approve allotment.
newsitem.headline: Kiwi Gold s/holders approve allotment.

text.p: Kiwi Gold Ltd said on Monday its shareholders had approved the allotment and issue of 25.1 million shares and 25.1 million options.

The company said it would seek quotation of the 25.1 million ordinary shares on the New Zealand Stock Exchange and the Australian Stock Exchange, but would not be seeking quotation of the 25.1 million options.
Kiwi Gold announced the proposed allotment last month when Texwood Pty, a company controlled by Ian Trahar, agreed to make an investment in the company of A$1.255 million.
"Mr Trahar is an Australian resident with extensive experience in the resource and finance industries. It is intended that Mr Trahar will become the Chairman of the company," Kiwi said at the time.
"The company has entered into an agreement to allot and issue 25.1 million ordinary shares and 25.1 million options in the company to Texwood.
"The ordinary shares will have an issue price of A$0.05 (to be converted into NZ dollars on the date of issue) resulting in an initial cash injection into the company of A$1.255 million," Kiwi said.
The issue will give Texwood 24.44 percent of the issued capital of the company (before the exercise of options).
Further funds may be invested by Texwood by electing to exercise its options.

Each option is exercisable for NZ$0.01 and will entitle Texwood to subscribe for one partly paid share with an issue price of A$0.062 (to be converted into NZ dollars on the date of issue) paid to NZ$0.01.
